changed.title: A fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit for the unrestricted shared-key witness moment at any order and fixed schedule
changed.statement:
∀ (k r h t : ℕ), 0 < h → h ≤ k → 0 < t →
  let rot := fun (d x : ℕ) => ((x <<< (d % k)) ||| (x >>> (k-d % k))) % 2^k
  let chi := fun (x : ℕ) => (List.range k).foldl (fun (acc i : ℕ) =>
    acc ||| ((xor (x.testBit i) (!(x.testBit ((i+1) % k)) && x.testBit ((i+2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let run := fun (masks : ℕ → Fin (2^k)) (col : Bool) (key name : ℕ) =>
    let gap : ℕ := if col then 2 else 1
    (List.range r).foldl (fun z j =>
      let mixed := z ^^^ rot gap z ^^^ rot (k-gap % k) z
      chi mixed ^^^ rot (if col then 3*(j+1)+1 else 2*j) key ^^^
        (masks (if col then r+j else j)).val) (rot (if col then 3 else 1) key ^^^ name)
  let B := if r = 0 then 2 else if r = 1 then 7 else 7*r-2
  let seam := fun (b : ℕ) => min k (h+b-k)
  let A := 2^(B+seam B+1)
  let scan := 2^(10*r+seam (4*r)+seam (6*r)+2) * Nat.choose (t+A-1) t
  let wiresIn := 2*r*k+2*h
  let bits := fun (len word : ℕ) => (List.range len).map (fun i => word.testBit i)
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (out : Fin ((t+2)*k+1) → Fin (wiresIn+C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack wiresIn C ∧
    C.output < wiresIn+C.size ∧
    C.size ≤ 1048576*((k+1)*(r+1)*(t+2))^4 * min (2^(3*k)) scan ∧
    ∀ (masks : ℕ → Fin (2^k)) (a b : Fin (2^h)),
      let input := (List.range (2*r)).flatMap (fun j => bits k (masks j).val) ++
        bits h a.val ++ bits h b.val
      let num := fun (x y : Fin (2^k)) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun key : Fin (2^k) =>
        (run masks false key.val x.val >>> (k-h)) = a.val ∧
        (run masks true key.val y.val >>> (k-h)) = b.val)).card
      let moment := ∑ x : Fin (2^k), ∑ y : Fin (2^k), (num x y)^t
      ∀ j : Fin ((t+2)*k+1), (C.wires input).getD (out j).val false = moment.testBit j.val
changed.unlocks: The first two orders count all ordered pairs of witnesses for a fixed schedule and give a certified density bound once evaluated. Higher orders measure concentrations on name pairs.
changed.context: Expand the power as t ordered keys sharing two names. At a tested site the raw memories for row name, column name and key have lengths 4r,6r,B, plus one entering bit each. Pin the g repeated residues of each track at every occurrence. For fixed name windows group keys by pinned bits, memory and entering bit. The histogram transfer weights each split by source multinomials. Sum over name bits, enforce both tests per occupied type, and double for each unused raw bit. Cap by counting keys per name pair directly. Estimate 4 to 8 hours.

changed.title: A weighted cover of guard-stop pairs gives the exact feedback menu budget
changed.statement:
∀ h : Nat, 0 < h →
  let bit := fun (u j : Nat) =>
    xor (u.testBit j) (!(u.testBit (j+1)) && u.testBit (j+2))
  let reply := fun u : Nat =>
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, if bit u j then 2^j else 0
  let fiber := fun z : Nat =>
    (Finset.range (2^(h+2))).filter (fun u => reply u = z)
  let dist := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (u v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => bit (u ^^^ p.1) p.2 != bit (v ^^^ p.1) p.2)).length
  let mask := fun (top r : Nat) => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r+1), 2^(top-2*i)
  let six := fun (r s : Nat) =>
    let a := mask h r
    let b := 2^(h+1)
    let c := mask (h-1) s
    [a, b, a ^^^ b, b ^^^ c, (a ^^^ b) ^^^ c, a ^^^ c]
  let wt := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => xor
      (v.testBit (p.2+1) && p.1.testBit (p.2+2))
      (v.testBit (p.2+2) && p.1.testBit (p.2+1)))).length
  let replies := Finset.range (2^h)
  let m := h/2
  let n := (h-1)/2
  ∀ (menu : Finset (List (Nat × Nat))) (b D target : Nat),
    (∀ Q ∈ menu, ∀ p ∈ Q, p.2 < h) →
    let good := fun (z : Nat) (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) =>
      (((fiber z).product (fiber z)).filter
        (fun uv => uv.1 ≠ uv.2 ∧ dist Q uv.1 uv.2 < D)).card = 0
    (∃ pick : Nat → List (Nat × Nat), replies.image pick ⊆ menu ∧
      (replies.image pick).card ≤ b ∧
      target ≤ (replies.filter (fun z => good z (pick z))).card) ↔
    ∃ bank : Finset (List (Nat × Nat)), bank.Nonempty ∧ bank ⊆ menu ∧ bank.card ≤ b ∧
      target ≤ ∑ r ∈ Finset.range (m+1), ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (n+1),
        if (bank.filter (fun Q => (six r s).all (fun v => decide (D ≤ wt Q v)) = true)).Nonempty
        then 2^(h-(min (r+1) m + min (s+1) n)) else 0
changed.unlocks: reduces the choice of a limited feedback menu to weighted coverage on quadratically many guard pairs
changed.context: Back-substitute from the two tail bits. The four strips differ by the six listed masks; expanding shifted comparisons gives their weights. A list covers a guard pair precisely when every weight reaches D. A stop fixes min(r+1,m) bits in a lane; the two lanes are disjoint. Sum the multiplicities of covered pairs. The image of any policy is a cover of its successes. Choose a covering list per type, with a default elsewhere. A smaller-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts distinct lists. Allow 60 to 120 minutes.

changed.title: A rectangular graph with exactly three missing diagonal edges has monotone gate minimum n plus m plus one
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat), 4 ≤ n → 4 ≤ m →
  let A := fun (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m) =>
    (64478 : Nat).testBit (4 * min u.val 3 + min v.val 3)
  PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (n + m + 1) ∧
    ¬ PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (n + m)
changed.unlocks: Settles the two-gate interval for the square family and gives the exact cost on every rectangular expansion.
changed.context: Permuting each side by [3,0,1,2] identifies the base with mask 31711 of checked cost nine. OR the extra row and column names for the upper bound. For the lower bound a full row accepts column zero and row zero rejects it. If the full row were ignored, monotonicity at the empty row bank would force that rejected entry. Normalize, fix one copy false and use deletion 376 to save a gate. Transpose for the columns, then iterate to four by four. Allow 180 to 300 minutes.
changed.sketch: Use the induced-subgraph gate bound on the first three rows and columns. Every kept line has a zero and a one. Every original line meets a nonfull opposite line, so a circuit of size s gives the zero-padded table a budget t with t+n+m at most s+6. Restrict it to the first four rows and columns without changing gates. Their row masks are 6,5,3,0, or mask 854, whose monotone minimum is seven. Thus s cannot be n+m. For the upper bound take the majority of the three matching row-column ORs, then OR in every extra wire.

Test an AND/OR witness against all 256 inputs, then prove that shorter circuits with at most one NOT fail using a gate lower bound or an exhaustive certificate. For a saving, exhibit the one-NOT circuit and exclude every shorter or equal-sized AND/OR circuit. The graph reader will inspect the shared wires and the input of the NOT in each saving. An equality removes this graph from the search for a saving.
